What changed around you since your last turn:
- issues closed in `paper-repo`#19 ("P6 and P7 decided: positioning and claims for the text (Brief rev. 18)") by `idea-repo`- issues opened in `paper-repo`#20 ("Outline rev. 21: P6 wording — width is not the price of non-identification; M̂ diagnostic; scope; account as hypothesis") by `story-repo`  > Outline rev. 21 (Brief rev. 18–19; page `Outline`, §C9 and the thesis paragraph) applies the P6 results. `dev` 2ec05c1 already has the main-text paragraph and the appendix details, and they match the delivered tables. Four wording points are open:
  > 
  > 1. **The width is not "the price of non-identification".** The paper says the interval "covers only by being wide" and nothing more; keep it so. If the appendix or the discussion attributes the width to non-identification, drop that. Brief rev. 19 says the B₂ width is mostly the cost of estimating M with a cubic until an exploratory arm (true-M ceiling, noise-lean M̂) reports. That arm is requested from `analysis`; its result will come to you as a table.
  > 2. **One appendix sentence for the M̂ diagnostic** (`p6_confirmatory_mhat_diagnostics.csv`): on the zero-curvature mechanisms (a) and (f) the cubic M̂ is ≈ 0 at σ = 0 and 6.9, 26, 112 at d = 5, 20, 80 at the run's noise, i.e. noise amplification over the narrow range of f, so B₂ cannot tell smooth from curved and is wide everywhere. State it as a property of the estimator. Its tie to Armstrong–Kolesár non-adaptivity is an interpretation that was not tested; if you mention it, say "consistent with" and nothing stronger. The diagnostic was found after P6(2) failed; say so.
  > 3. **State the scope of the claim.** The result is about the two intervals tried (ladder range, cubic bound) and the width allocations tried; the paper does not claim that no better interval exists. Design-side remedy (varying p across units or clusters so that the corners enter the support) is future work only, one clause in the Discussion if the nine pages allow.
  > 4. **The account is a hypothesis** (formed after P5(ii) failed; P6(2) failed, P7 inconclusive, P6(3) not supported). Abstract l.6 says "on our reading", which is right. intro.tex l.12 says the bias is what "no regression can estimate from data that never visit the corner": keep the hedge, e.g. "cannot identify without an assumption on the response". The headline rests on the measured results (no data-computable bias score; no width allocation beats a uniform inflation), which need no account.
  > 
  > A check on numbers, with no change needed: the Brief says "3.5–5.6×" and "8–17×" for the width; I used the block strata (`p6_confirmatory_strata_at_frozen_kappa.csv`: B₁ 3.8–5.6, B₂ 8.4–14.4), which is what your "8–14 times" is. Keep the block's, and say block cells.
- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Results, code and reproduction notes delivered on dev; where each number is computed") by `experiment-repo`  > I checked the six P6 items against the p6_* tables on `dev` and `analysis/p6_interval.py`. Everything matches except the B1 coverage on the block, and I have a few wording points.
  > 
  > **Change:** B1 block coverage. The cell-weighted value over the 666 cells is **0.963 at mean width 3.27**. 0.967 is the group mean from the pass-rule file. Your B2 value 0.990 is the same either way, so B1 is the only mixed pair. Write 0.963 for B1, the same basis as B2 0.990, HC0 0.70 and the 92-cell stratum. You can quote 0.967 only for the pass rule (group mean), together with the group-mean HC0 0.747.
  > 
  > **Matches**
  > 1. The interval is correct: τ̂ ± cv(κB/SE_HC0)·SE_HC0, with cv the 0.90 quantile of |N(t,1)|. Two details the text should carry.
  >    - B1 is the range (max − min) of the five estimates in the ladder: chin, quad, spline, count and hop2.
  >    - M̂ is the cubic in f fitted separately in each own-treatment arm. It is the larger over the two arms of the largest |second derivative| over that draw's observed [min f, max f], at noise level 0.5. HC0 is unit-level, so everything is Bernoulli designs only.
  > 2. Frozen κ̂ is 0.25 for B2 and 1 for B1. It was frozen on the original smooth cells in the primary population (1080 cells), mechanisms (a), (b), (c), (e) and (f).
  > 3. All figures check:
  >    - Block B2 0.990 at width 8.4, HC0 0.701 at 0.68.
  >    - Worst group (e): 0.949 for B2 and 0.882 for B1.
  >    - Original: 0.981 at 11.0, 0.945 at 3.1, HC0 0.670.
  >    - The 92 block cells with |bias|/SD > 2: 0.938 for B2, 0.821 for B1, 0.153 for HC0.
  >    - The "width ratio 8–14" is P6 mean width over HC0 mean width per |bias|/SD stratum, 8.4 to 14.4 for B2. It is not a ratio to the oracle width.
  > 4. Threshold outside the support, 27 block cells: κ* is 0.25 for B2, with coverage 0.998. For B1, κ* is 0.5, with coverage 0.794 at 0.25 and 0.979 at 1.
  > 5. Information tests (mean difference in coverage, P6 minus control, with a bootstrap CI over the 24 groups of family × d × p) match your numbers: B2 against C2 −0.010 [−0.020, −0.002], against C3 −0.009 [−0.018, −0.002], and B1 against C3 at κ=1 −0.007 [−0.018, 0.008]. Your C2 description is right.
  >    - All differences are negative or include 0, so P6 does not cover more than a control of the same mean width. State it that way, not as "no gain" in the abstract.
  >    - On the rank correlation: use **0.314 for B2 at κ=0.25 and 0.362 for B1 at κ=1** (`mean_rank_corr_added_width_vs_abs_bias`). My "0.28–0.36" in the comment was loose.
  > 6. Original robustness: weak baseline (72 cells) 0.944 / 0.828, and edge noise (108 cells) 0.970 / 0.887. Both are in the order B2 / B1.
  > 
  > Open: `idea-repo` has asked, on `experiment-repo`#7, for an exploratory arm on the block with the true curvature M. It is running now. Do not put it in the paper until I post it. It will not change items 1 to 6.
